summary: D12 REPRODUCES AND SURVIVES BEING PUSHED ON. The supervisor's core measurement is confirmed and extended from one tensor to the whole composed system: 9 configuration arms, each built twice in FRESH processes through the real spine.compose.compose(), digested over 363 values (36 of them nn.Module parameters/buffers, plus every Fabric/World/Store/Partition/Vocabulary/Stream/Plan/Manifest field) -- IDENTICAL in every arm; RUN_SEED 0/1/7 give torch_seed 3734753547471956429 / 1763737848520504121 / 3401938060292914317 and three distinct outputs. Nothing draws from torch's global generator before process_setup (measured, not assumed: importing all 23 modules leaves torch.random.get_rng_state() bit-identical, and the state at process_setup's entry equals the state after import). The read-back is REAL, not an echo -- proved by hijacking torch.manual_seed to seed 424242, whereupon Process.torch_seed reports 424242 and not the derived value. derive_seed is pure: called twice it returns the same number, rng.issued() stays {}, process_setup runs twice in one process, and 'torch.global' appears in neither issued() nor compose.RNG_SUBSYSTEMS (while rng_for('torch.global', 0) does raise on the second call, so option (b)'s rejection is sound). The contract-spelling claim is exactly right, verified by running tests/test_contract.py::_split_items on both spellings. FOUR THINGS GO BEYOND THE RULING. (1) D12's limitation is real and is now EXHIBITED rather than stated: with the global stream reset to a fixed position before the forward, LM_LAYERS=2 vs 4 at LM_DROPOUT=0.2 moves a downstream global consumer (nn.Linear weights 5f87be0f2321e508 vs 36dc18c1f2e82308; next torch.rand(3) [0.180,0.733,0.012] vs [0.621,0.406,0.741]), and the LM_DROPOUT=0.0 control makes both arms IDENTICAL (31a48739b3d15e14, [0.415,0.440,0.095]) -- so the shift is the dropout draw COUNT and nothing else. (2) But D12's sentence 'still moves the numbers of every package downstream of it' is WIDER THAN THE TREE: every package's build-time constructor draws ARE consumed from the global and are then fully overwritten from its own named stream, so the build-time half of the channel is inert -- inserting 1 or 3 extra global draws between LM.build_model and the rest of compose leaves all 363 built values byte-identical while moving LM.encode, and the real-lever version (LM_LAYERS 2 vs 4) moves nothing outside LM at all. The channel is live but SINGLE-ENDED at HEAD: LM is the only package that draws from the global at runtime. (3) Process.torch_seed is a declared firing surface that NOTHING reads -- grep finds no consumer in src/, tests/ or docs/ -- and after a later torch.manual_seed(999) the record says 3734753547471956429 while torch says 999, with nothing noticing. That is exactly the standing of its siblings tf32_applied and amp_state, which have no reader either, so it is not a regression. (4) The tree-wide spelling hunt found the hazard in THREE more entry points, all naming a lever they genuinely read in the form the harvester drops -- but no lever loses its credit, because K4 aggregates per PACKAGE and the UNCONSUMED table is empty, so no verdict changes at HEAD. Full suite green after all work; I edited nothing.

findings.detail: THE MEASUREMENT REPRODUCES AND IS MUCH WIDER THAN ONE TENSOR. Harness: a fresh subprocess per configuration, importing src/spine/compose.py and running the real compose(), with spine.compose.System subclassed so the PARTIALLY BUILT record survives the NotImplementedError that stops the root. compose() reaches stage 'valve' at HEAD and raises 'CAP.startup_refusals: P4 (capacity) fills this in'; the digest therefore covers LM.build_model's model, SIG.build's encoder, FAB.build's Population (A, B, cent, halt_b and all eight nn.Linear/LayerNorm modules), WORLD.build, MEM.open_store's Store, DOM.open_partition's Partition, CAP.new_valve's Valve, plus LM.resolve's geometry, TOK.build_vocabulary's Vocabulary, DATA.draw_stream's Stream, TOK.tokenize's Segmentation, DATA.data_plan and the geometry manifest -- 363 recorded values, 36 of them named nn.Module parameters or buffers. TWO FRESH PROCESSES PER ARM, all IDENTICAL on torch_seed, on the 363-value digest and on two LM.encode() calls: gru LM_DROPOUT=0.2 (torch_seed 3734753547471956429, tdig 34acff0aeb14dd4b, enc1 26905f117c4d32e7 sum 5.410000); transformer LM_LAYERS=2 (tdig 1bd5454c9b4e68e7, enc1 79018f686bb426de sum -36.204098); transformer LM_LAYERS=4 LM_DROPOUT=0.3 RUN_SEED=3 (torch_seed 5332998230351403952, enc1 9091885290ff2252 sum -457.526062); SIG_MODE=bigram (tdig 7ced830ac9477b4d); TOK_DROPOUT=0.3 (tdig 8deffb709e208d75, enc1 UNCHANGED at 26905f117c4d32e7, which is the right answer -- TOK draws from its own named stream and does not touch the global); RUN_TF32=0 and RUN_AMP=bf16 (both identical to the shipped arm, tdig 34acff0aeb14dd4b). SEED SEPARATION HOLDS: RUN_SEED 0/1/7 -> torch_seed 3734753547471956429 / 1763737848520504121 / 3401938060292914317 and tdig 34acff0aeb14dd4b / 570a59a375fb52e8 / 522e9c32b472768c, so the fix did not collapse every seed onto one sequence. The seed 0 and seed 7 numbers match the ones .rework/DECISIONS.md D12 and .rework/audits/close_train_seed.json report. A LARGER SURFACE STILL: with CAP.startup_refusals neutralised IN THE HARNESS ONLY (nothing in src/ edited), compose() runs on through OPT.build to stage 'clock' and stops at 'RUN.new_clock: P4 (train) fills this in'; 463 values, digest 0b07280c98fbe649 in both of two fresh processes, zero differing keys.
findings.repro: Scratch harness OUTSIDE the repo at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad/vseed/build.py and matrix.py; `python3 matrix.py` prints the nine rows above, each 'IDENTICAL'. build.py takes the environment as a JSON argv, clears os.environ, subclasses spine.compose.System to capture the partial record, walks every attribute (following __slots__ as well as __dict__, since Population/World/Store/Partition/Vocabulary/Stream are all __slots__ classes) and blake2b-digests every tensor's exact float64 values plus every scalar field.

findings.detail: 'BEFORE ANY PACKAGE IS BUILT' IS LITERALLY TRUE, AND NOTHING DRAWS FIRST. Three separate checks. (a) IMPORT TIME: in a fresh process, torch.random.get_rng_state() captured immediately after `import torch` and again after importing spine.lever, spine.rng, spine.units, spine.derive, spine.gate, spine.wire, spine.registry, spine.init, spine.assemble, spine.compose and all thirteen packages' api modules one at a time -- the state is bit-identical throughout and no single import moves it. That matters because torch.manual_seed RESETS the generator, so the only way a pre-seed draw could hurt is a value RETAINED from before the reset (a module-level tensor, a default argument evaluated at import); an AST walk of every module-level statement in src/*/api.py and src/spine/*.py finds no tensor construction and no call at all outside constants, dict and tuple literals. (b) BETWEEN IMPORT AND THE CALL: process_setup was wrapped to snapshot get_rng_state() at entry; it equals the post-import state on every run, so spine.assemble.build()'s config resolution -- everything compose() does before this row -- draws nothing. (c) INSIDE THE FUNCTION: the source reads `seed = int(run.seed)` then `torch.manual_seed(_rng.derive_seed("torch.global", seed))` as the first executable statement, three lines BEFORE `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = tf32`. An AST sweep for every RNG-initialising nn constructor (Linear, Embedding, GRU, LSTM, RNN, TransformerEncoderLayer, TransformerEncoder, MultiheadAttention, Conv*, Bilinear, EmbeddingBag) across src/*/api.py places ALL of them inside src/fabric/api.py::build, src/lm/api.py::_LM.__init__, src/sig/api.py::_Encoder.__init__ and src/world/api.py::build -- i.e. inside compose()'s build rows, every one of which runs after this function. python's global `random` module is imported in exactly one file, src/spine/rng.py, and is reached only through Rng, so there is no companion global to seed; numpy is not installed on this box at all.
findings.repro: /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/vseed/imp.py prints 'STATE_CHANGED_BY []' and 'STATE_IDENTICAL_OVERALL True'; build.py reports state_unchanged_import_to_process_setup=True on every arm; `grep -rn '^import random\|^from random' src/ --include=*.py` returns only src/spine/rng.py.

findings.detail: Process.torch_seed IS GENUINELY READ BACK, NOT AN ECHO OF THE WRITE -- proved by making the write disagree with the request. torch.manual_seed was replaced, in the module namespace process_setup actually calls through, with a function that ignores its argument and seeds 424242. process_setup then returned Process.torch_seed == 424242 (and torch.initial_seed() == 424242), NOT derive_seed('torch.global', 0) == 3734753547471956429. An echo would have reported the derived number. This is the strongest form of the check because it separates the two candidate implementations by their observable behaviour rather than by reading the source.
findings.repro: /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/vseed/readback.py -> 'D3 with torch.manual_seed hijacked to seed 424242 -> Process.torch_seed = 424242 | torch.initial_seed() = 424242 | READ-BACK'.

findings.detail: PURE, MINTS NOTHING, AND THE LABEL STAYS OUT OF THE REGISTER -- all four sub-claims run rather than read. derive_seed('torch.global', 0) called twice returns 3734753547471956429 both times and leaves spine.rng.issued() == {}. src/train/api.py::process_setup called TWICE in one process returns the same torch_seed both times, raises nothing, and still leaves issued() == {}. 'torch.global' is not in src/spine/compose.py::RNG_SUBSYSTEMS, whose live value is ('lm','sig','fabric','memory','domains','world','tok.dropout','data.synth','data.holdout','eval'), and it never appears in issued() on a real compose() -- the seventeen names a full build mints are data.holdout, data.stream.e0, data.synth, data.synth.c, data.synth.eng, data.synth.num, data.synth.py, domains, eval, fabric, lm, lm.init, memory, sig, tok.dropout, tok.dropout.mint, world. The rejected alternative behaves as D12 says it would: rng_for('torch.global', 0) succeeds once (Rng with seed 3734753547471956429 -- the same number, so the label and the derivation agree) and the SECOND call raises RngError 'stream torch.global was already issued for seed 0', and it does put 'torch.global' into issued(). So derive_seed is the only one of the two that keeps process_setup callable twice AND keeps issued() meaning what src/spine/compose.py's RNG_SUBSYSTEMS comment says it means.
findings.repro: /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/vseed/readback.py (the four D4 lines) and a five-line script calling spine.rng.rng_for('torch.global', 0) twice.

findings.detail: THE STATED LIMITATION IS REAL AND IS NOW EXHIBITED, BUT ITS SENTENCE IS WIDER THAN THE TREE. EXHIBITED, first: after compose(), the global stream was reset to a fixed position (torch.manual_seed(12345)) in EVERY arm so that any later difference can only be draw COUNT, then one LM.encode() was run, then a downstream consumer read the shared stream. LM_ARCH=transformer LM_DROPOUT=0.2, LM_LAYERS=2 vs LM_LAYERS=4: the downstream nn.Linear(4,4) weights digest 5f87be0f2321e508 vs 36dc18c1f2e82308 and the following torch.rand(3) is [0.18013722,0.73333818,0.01200253] vs [0.62094098,0.40641177,0.740619]. THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES IT A MEASUREMENT: the same two depths at LM_DROPOUT=0.0 give the IDENTICAL downstream values (31a48739b3d15e14, [0.41499043,0.43999398,0.09452492]), so the shift is the number of DROPOUT draws and not anything else about depth. A second forward shifts it again (b21c5279000ab0a8, [0.00938696,0.40470266,0.9964624]). That is D12's channel, alive, driven by an LM lever, with no wire covering it. NOW THE NARROWING. D12 says 'Adding a package that draws from the global, or reordering two that do, still moves the numbers of every package downstream of it'. The BUILD-TIME half of that is not true of this tree today, and I checked it two ways rather than reasoning about it. (i) SYNTHETIC: inserting 1 or 3 extra global draws (torch.rand(n), no generator=) between LM.build_model's return and the rest of compose() -- exactly what n extra dropout masks would do -- leaves all 363 built values byte-identical (digest 34acff0aeb14dd4b in all three runs) while moving LM.encode (26905f117c4d32e7 -> 773820fb538ba090 -> 0b850362297af161). (ii) REAL LEVER: LM_LAYERS 2 vs 4, which changes how many draws nn.TransformerEncoderLayer's constructors take from the global by a large amount, moves NOTHING outside LM -- zero non-LM keys differ; and LM_ARCH gru vs transformer moves only store.lm_kind and its gate, which is the DECLARED hand-off `lm_kind=lm.arch` in spine/compose.py's MEM.open_store call, not a leak. The reason is that every package that constructs an nn.Module then overwrites every parameter from its OWN named stream -- src/lm/api.py::build_model's named_parameters loop, src/sig/api.py::_Encoder.__init__, src/fabric/api.py::build's pop.modules loop, src/world/api.py::build's encoder/world_proj/qproj loop. AND THE RUNTIME HALF IS SINGLE-ENDED: an exhaustive grep for every RNG-consuming torch call in src/ (rand, randn, randint, randperm, multinomial, bernoulli, normal, poisson, *_like, nn.init.*, in-place *_ samplers, functional dropout) returns exactly three hits, all in src/sig/api.py and all passing generator=; the only implicit consumers left are nn.Dropout and nn.TransformerEncoderLayer's internals, and an AST sweep places every RNG-initialising module constructor inside a build entry point that runs before any forward. So at HEAD LM is the ONLY package that draws from the global generator at runtime, which is why the downstream consumer in the demonstration above has to be a probe. The limitation is correctly identified and correctly rejected as unfixable here; the claim that is wider than the evidence is the scope of 'every package downstream', and the practical reading is that the channel arms the moment a SECOND package draws from the global at runtime, or a package is built lazily after a forward.
findings.repro: /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/vseed/channel.py (five configurations, the numbers above) and build.py's PERTURB_DRAWS knob (p0.json/p1.json/p3.json -> zero differing keys, differing encode); `python3 -c "..."` diff of tr.json vs tr4.json -> 'NON-LM differing: []'.

findings.detail: THE DID IT FIRE SURFACE IS DECLARED AND HAS NO READER, AND THE RECORD GOES SILENTLY STALE IF ANYTHING RESEEDS AFTERWARDS. `grep -rn torch_seed src/ tests/ docs/ tools/` returns hits ONLY inside src/train/api.py itself plus one prose line in .rework/DECISIONS.md -- no check, no report, no other package reads Process.torch_seed. Reseeding after the fact: process_setup() then torch.manual_seed(999) leaves Process.torch_seed == 3734753547471956429 while torch.initial_seed() == 999, and nothing anywhere notices -- no gate, no warning, no exception. THAT IS THE CORRECT SEMANTICS FOR A SNAPSHOT and it is what the docstring's own sentence describes ('a reader checks it against torch.initial_seed() directly' -- a human reader, at a console), but the docstring's stronger sentence, that torch_seed 'is what makes seeding that generator a DECLARED setting rather than a silent global side effect', is true only once something declares it out loud. WHAT KEEPS THIS AT low AND NOT A DEFECT: its two siblings on the same record are in exactly the same position. `grep -rn 'tf32_applied\|amp_state' src/ tests/ docs/` outside src/train/api.py returns NOTHING either. So this is the P5 reporting layer not existing yet, uniformly, and not a hole opened by D12. It becomes a real defect only if the banner P5 writes prints tf32_applied and amp_state and leaves torch_seed out.
findings.repro: /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/vseed/readback.py line D3b: 'after a later torch.manual_seed(999): Process.torch_seed = 3734753547471956429 torch.initial_seed() = 999 -> record and reality DISAGREE'; plus the two greps quoted above.

findings.detail: THE AGENT'S SPELLING CLAIM IS EXACTLY RIGHT, AND IT MATTERS. Running the real parser, not reasoning about the regex: the SHIPPED line 'device, tf32, amp, seed (new on 2026-09-03; ...)' splits to ['device','tf32','amp','seed'] and all four survive the bare-identifier filter, so `seed` is credited. The line the referring report .rework/audits/fix_lm.json proposed, 'device, tf32, amp, seed -- new on 2026-09-03; ...', splits to ['device','tf32','amp','seed -- new on 2026-09-03; the process-global torch generator is\n seeded from it through spine/rng.py::derive_seed'] and the fourth item fails re.fullmatch(r'[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*'), so `seed` would have been DROPPED and RUN_SEED would have earned no K4 credit from this entry point. The reason is _split_items' own documented behaviour: it is depth-aware on parentheses and strips a parenthetical with re.sub(r'\(.*', '', it), so '(<note>)' is removed and the bare identifier is left, while a '--' note is simply part of the item text. The live tree agrees: tests/test_contract.py::stub_reads('src')['RUN'] harvests {'amp','bench','device','epochs','none','profile','seed','tf32'} -- `seed` present.
findings.repro: /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/vseed/k4scan.py, which imports tests/test_contract.py and calls _split_items and stub_reads directly.

findings.detail: THE TREE-WIDE SWEEP THE TASK ASKED FOR: the dropped-item form EXISTS in three other entry points, all of which genuinely read the lever they name -- but NO lever loses its credit, so no check changes verdict at HEAD, and I will not inflate this into the tree-wide defect it is not. Method: for every LEVERS READ / WIRES READ block in every file tests/test_contract.py::stub_reads actually opens (src/<pkg>/api.py for all thirteen packages), every item _split_items produces that fails the bare-identifier filter was collected, and its leading identifier was cross-checked against that package's declared lever set from tests/test_contract.py::declared_levers. 29 dropped items exist; 26 are ordinary prose after 'none' or 'none directly' and are correctly dropped. THE THREE THAT ARE NOT: (1) src/tok/api.py::build_vocabulary -- its LEVERS READ line ends '..., max_bytes, dropout' and the NEXT line begins '# cand_window, mint_pmin and mint_novel are NOT read here', so the first comma the splitter sees is the one after 'cand_window' and the item becomes 'dropout\n# cand_window', which is dropped. The function spans lines 190-423 and reads `float(tok.dropout)` twice inside that span, so this is a real read whose declaration is invisible to the harvester -- and it is the LAST name on the line, which is what the '#'-continuation form always eats. (2) src/lm/api.py::encode -- 'ctx -- ONLY on the pos-overflow refusal path, to print LM_CTX beside...' is dropped; the body does read lm.ctx. (3) src/lm/api.py::decode -- 'mask_dead_rows -- NOT `vocab_slots` or `compose`, which the body takes off...' is dropped; the body does read lm.mask_dead_rows. WHY NOTHING FAILS: tests/test_contract.py::check_k4_levers_have_readers aggregates the harvest PER PACKAGE, not per entry point, and each of the three levers is credited by a clean sibling line in the same file (TOK.dropout by TOK.tokenize's 'LEVERS READ: mode, dropout'; LM.ctx and LM.mask_dead_rows by LM.resolve's and LM.state_dict's lists). tests/test_contract.py::doc_unconsumed returns the EMPTY set, so no lever is sitting in the UNCONSUMED table while an entry point silently claims to read it either. K5 is untouched -- zero WIRES READ items are dropped anywhere. So: the hazard is real and recurs, the agent was right to avoid it, and it is one clean-sibling deletion away from becoming a false 'armed-but-inert' verdict on a lever an operator can really set. It is not currently costing the tree anything, and I found no case where it is.
findings.repro: /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/vseed/k4scan2.py (enumerates all 29 dropped items with the entry point that produced each) and k4scan3.py (cross-checks each against declared_levers, stub_reads and doc_unconsumed; every line prints 'CREDITED ELSEWHERE'). The reads were confirmed by AST: build_vocabulary 190-423 with `float(tok.dropout)` inside; encode 475-620 reading lm.ctx; decode 623-732 reading lm.mask_dead_rows.

findings.detail: THE CUDA ARM IS UNTESTED AND SEEDING ALONE WOULD NOT BE ENOUGH THERE. torch.cuda.is_available() is False on this box, so every number in this report is CPU. Two things follow that the ruling does not say. First, the coverage claim rests on the installed torch's own docstring, which I quoted rather than assumed: inspect.getsource(torch.manual_seed) at 2.13.0+cu130 begins 'Sets the seed for generating random numbers on all devices'. Second, and not stated anywhere in D12 or in .rework/audits/close_train_seed.json: a seed is NECESSARY but not SUFFICIENT for two CUDA runs to agree. process_setup sets torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 and torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 and nothing else; it does not call torch.use_deterministic_algorithms, so non-deterministic CUDA kernels (atomics in scatter/index_add-style reductions, which MEM and DOM's slot machinery is the natural place for) remain free to reorder. torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark is False by default at this version -- checked, so autotuning is NOT an additional source here. This is a scope note, not a request to widen the function: the honest reading is that Process.torch_seed proves the SEED matched and, exactly as the docstring already says, two runs reporting the same torch_seed that still disagree have some OTHER non-determinism -- on CUDA there is a named family of them and nobody has ruled it out.
findings.repro: python3 -c "import torch, inspect; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available()); print([l for l in inspect.getsource(torch.manual_seed).splitlines() if 'all' in l][:1]); print(torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark)" -> '2.13.0+cu130 False', the 'all devices' line, 'False'. grep for use_deterministic_algorithms in src/train/api.py returns nothing.

findings.detail: PRE-EXISTING AND NOT CAUSED BY D12, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-DISCOVERED A THIRD TIME. The contract document's 'Executable today' paragraph still says compose() 'stops at the first unimplemented one with NotImplementedError: RUN.process_setup: P4 (train) fills this in', and the same stale claim appears twice more -- in the document's CAP pin-clock section ('compose() stops at RUN.process_setup long before the valve') and in src/capacity/api.py::<module>'s header. MEASURED: RUN.process_setup has had a body since before this change; compose(environ={...}) now runs through the process, resume, refuse, geometry, corpus, vocab, gate, plan, stream, segment, model, signature, fabric, world, store and partition rows and stops at stage 'valve' with 'NotImplementedError: CAP.startup_refusals: P4 (capacity) fills this in'. It was already filed once, in .rework/audits/readme_r1_partial.json, whose caveat field says the doc's named function 'is not' the stop. I am reporting it because two of the three sites are in files I do not own and because D12's change did not make it worse -- it is simply still true and still uncorrected. NOT MINE TO FIX: I may not edit, and src/capacity/api.py is another agent's this run (.rework/audits/v_cap_eval.json is untracked beside mine).
